original_interpretation: ASML 2025 AR risk factors: alternative production capacity may not be available if a major disruption hit one of its few manufacturing sites.
evidence_found: "These facilities may be subject to disruption for various reasons ... Alternative production capacity may not be available if a major disruption were to occur." (ASML AR 2025, Risk factors, 'We are dependent on the continued operation of a limited number of manufacturing facilities', p. 68)
notes: Risk-factor disclosure correctly typed as reported_claim.

original_interpretation: ASML shipped NXE:3800E at full spec in 2025: 220 wph, 37% above NXE:3600D; installed systems upgraded to same spec.
evidence_found: "In 2025, we shipped TWINSCAN NXE:3800E systems to our customers at full specification, which includes 220 wafers-per-hour throughput – a 37% improvement compared to the TWINSCAN NXE:3600D ... We completed field upgrades to bring systems that were already in customer fabs to the same specifications." (AR 2025, Our products and services, p. 17)
notes: Rated/spec throughput, a company claim. AR p.174 energy table also lists NXE:3800E ATP throughput 220 (2024) and 230 wph (2025 measurement).

original_interpretation: ASML shipped first EXE:5200B in early April 2025, 175 wph, 60% above EXE:5000.
evidence_found: "In early April 2025, we shipped our first TWINSCAN EXE:5200B system – the successor to the TWINSCAN EXE:5000 – ready to be used in high- volume manufacturing. At 175 wafers per hour, it offers 60% higher productivity compared to the TWINSCAN EXE:5000" (AR 2025, p. 16)
notes: Same page: "We expect our TWINSCAN EXE platform to start supporting high-volume manufacturing in 2027." 175 wph is a spec, not a measured fleet average.

original_interpretation: EXE systems recognized in sales diluted ASML's 2025 gross margin.
evidence_found: "Gross profit and gross margin increased, mainly driven by a favorable NXE product mix and higher net service and field option sales and margins. These positive effects on gross margin were partially offset by the dilutive impact of EXE systems recognized in sales." (AR 2025, Financial performance KPIs, p. 54; same wording p. 50)
notes: Context: 2025 gross margin rose overall (50.5% to 51.8%); EXE only partially offset the increase.

original_interpretation: ASML CEO: several customers say 0.55 NA EUV is more mature than 0.33 NA was at the same stage.
evidence_found: "We have also achieved outstanding progress on EUV 0.55 NA, with a number of customers reporting that it is now more mature than EUV 0.33 NA was at the same stage of development." (AR 2025, In conversation with our CEO, p. 7)
notes: Second-hand customer opinion relayed by the vendor; reported_claim is the right type.

original_interpretation: Inference: ASML filings show 6 EXE recognized through end-2025 (2 in 2024, 4 in 2025), consistent with press reports of <12 High-NA units worldwide by March 2026; ASML publishes no cumulative High-NA count.
evidence_found: AR 2025 Note 2 'Net system sales per technology': "EXE — — 2 465.0 4 1,156.9" (2023/2024/2025 units, EUR m), p. 280; p. 54: "We recognized four EXE and 44 NXE systems in sales in 2025 compared to two EXE and 42 NXE systems in 2024." TrendForce 2026-03-19: "Reuters adds that the system costs roughly $400 million and is one of fewer than a dozen units worldwide."
notes: Arithmetic and reasoning hold. Searched the AR 2025 text for a cumulative EXE shipment/installed-base count and found none (it gives only '>400,000 wafers' run on High NA, p. 8). The 'fewer than a dozen' figure is Reuters via TrendForce (tier 2/3 relay), so the cross-check is weak.

original_interpretation: Inference: among ASML (327), Canon (234) and Nikon (27, FY to Mar-2026) lithography units, shares are ~56%/40%/5%; ASML's value share is far higher (sole EUV, most ArFi).
evidence_found: ASML AR 2025 p. 65: "(327 units in 2025, 418 units in 2024 and 449 units in 2023)"; p. 280 per-technology units sum to 327 (EXE 4, NXE 44, ArFi 131, ArF dry 16, KrF 78, i-line 54). Canon slide 20: total "73 234 224". Nikon FY2026/3 table total "27". 327/588=55.6%, 234/588=39.8%, 27/588=4.6%. AR p. 16: "ASML is currently the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography systems."
notes: Arithmetic correct. Caveats: ASML's 327 includes used systems (the technology table totals net system sales of new + used); Nikon's 27 includes 5 refurbished; Nikon is FY Apr-Mar. Nikon's May-2026 deck now reports CY2025 market scale as 570 (actual, see new claim from this batch), which is BELOW the 588 three-vendor sum, so vendor counts and Nikon's market definition are not fully comparable.

original_interpretation: ASML: nearly all PAS 5500 systems (introduced early 1990s) remain in active use, mainly in 'More than Moore' markets.
evidence_found: "Our PAS 5500 lithography system, introduced in the early 1990s, played a pivotal role in ASML's rise ... Despite their age, nearly all of these systems remain in active use, particularly in the mainstream 'More than Moore' semiconductor market." (AR 2025, Managing our installed base, p. 19)

original_interpretation: ASML competes mainly with Canon and Nikon in DUV; a weaker yen vs euro has increased price competition.
evidence_found: "We compete primarily with Canon and Nikon in respect of DUV systems. Both have substantial financial resources and broad patent portfolios. ... adverse market conditions, long-term overcapacity or a decrease in the value of the Japanese yen in relation to the euro have increased and could continue to increase price-based competition" (AR 2025, Risk factors, p. 64)
notes: Yen weakness is listed alongside adverse market conditions and overcapacity as joint causes.

original_interpretation: Intel FY2025 10-K: may pause/discontinue Intel 14A and successors without a significant external 14A customer; Intel 4, 3, 18A, 14A use EUV.
evidence_found: "particularly those utilizing EUV lithography such as Intel 4, Intel 3, Intel 18A, Intel 14A and future nodes, require substantial capital investment." ... "if we are unable to secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, we may pause or discontinue our pursuit of Intel 14A and successor leading-edge process technologies." (10-K FY ended 2025-12-27, Item 1)
notes: Read from the SEC EDGAR primary document. The 10-K also says: "We have been unsuccessful to date in securing any significant external foundry customers for any of our nodes" (Risk Factors).

original_interpretation: ASML: 2026 low-NA EUV capacity ~65 and DUV immersion ~130 systems; +30% each for 2027; investigating another +30% for 2028.
evidence_found: "we are planning to add 30% to our 2026 low NA EUV capacity of around 65 for 2027, and we are investigating to increase capacity with another 30% for 2028. Similarly, we plan to add 30% to our 2026 DUV immersion capacity of around 130 for 2027, and we are investigating to increase capacity with another 30% in 2028." (ASML Q2 2026 press release, CEO statement)
notes: Plans and capacity statements, correctly reported_claim.

original_interpretation: ASML sold 67 new + 12 used litho systems in Q1 2026 and 86 new + 5 used in Q2 2026.
evidence_found: Table: "New lithography systems sold (units) | 67 | 86"; "Used lithography systems sold (units) | 12 | 5" (columns Q1 2026 | Q2 2026; ASML Q2 2026 press release, 2026-07-15)
notes: Also matches the Q1 2026 release (asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2026/q1-2026-financial-results, opened this run): Q1 2026 new 67, used 12; Q4 2025 new 94, used 8. Unaudited quarterly figures.

original_interpretation: ASML guides 2026 total net sales of EUR 43-45 bn (raised July 2026).
evidence_found: "ASML now expects 2026 total net sales to be between €43 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin between 54% and 56%" (Q2 2026 press release, 2026-07-15)
notes: 'Raised' confirmed: the Q1 2026 release (2026-04-15, opened this run) said "between €36 billion and €40 billion". Forward-looking guidance; Q3 2026 results not yet published as of 2026-10-01.

original_interpretation: ASML (July 2026): Intel Foundry in HVM of a subset of Panther Lake on High-NA for specific 18A layers in Oregon, yields matched to NXE.
evidence_found: "Intel Foundry has entered high-volume manufacturing for a subset of Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 3 processors, code-named Panther Lake, using ASML's EXE High NA EUV technology" ... "Specific Intel 18A layers are now dual-qualified on High NA EUV in Oregon, with product shipping to customers at yields matched to the NXE platform" (ASML release, 2026-07-15)
notes: Checked against the GlobeNewswire copy and the original on asml.com (asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2026/high-na-euv-reaches-new-readiness-milestone, opened this run); wording identical, so no new source added. 'Dual-qualified' means the layers can also run on NXE; this is not High-NA-only production.

original_interpretation: ASML: Intel completed integration of the first commercial High-NA system at Hillsboro in 2024 and was first to install and pass acceptance of EXE:5200B.
evidence_found: "In 2024, Intel and ASML completed integration of the industry's first commercial High NA EUV lithography system at the company's Hillsboro, Oregon, R&D site. Intel Foundry was also the first company to install and pass acceptance testing of the second generation, TWINSCAN EXE:5200B" (ASML release, 2026-07-15)
notes: The source says 'Intel and ASML' completed integration (joint), a small wording difference.

original_interpretation: June 2024: ASML and imec expected High-NA HVM in 2025-2026.
evidence_found: "The opening of the joint ASML-imec High NA EUV Lab represents a milestone in preparing High NA EUV for high-volume manufacturing – anticipated to happen in the 2025–2026 timeframe." (ASML/imec announcement, 2024-06-03)
notes: Correct as a dated historical expectation. Later ASML guidance moved it: AR 2025 p. 16 "We expect our TWINSCAN EXE platform to start supporting high-volume manufacturing in 2027" (SRC-0161). Do not use this claim as the current timeline.

original_interpretation: ASML and imec opened joint High-NA lab in Veldhoven June 2024 around prototype EXE:5000, giving early access; printed 10 nm dense lines (20 nm pitch) on MOR.
evidence_found: "announced the opening of the High NA EUV Lithography Lab in Veldhoven ... access to the first prototype High NA EUV scanner (TWINSCAN EXE:5000) and surrounding processing and metrology tools." ... "showing for the first time ever 10 nm dense lines (20 nm pitch) printed in Veldhoven on metal oxide resists (MORs) using the 0.55 NA EUV prototype scanner." (2024-06-03)
notes: Lab opening is fact. The 'first time ever' patterning result is the companies' own claim; claim_type 'fact' is acceptable for the event but the imaging result should be read as reported.

original_interpretation: ASML agreed Oct 2012 to acquire Cymer for ~EUR 1.95 bn cash and stock to accelerate EUV.
evidence_found: "ASML will acquire all outstanding shares of Cymer in a cash-and-stock transaction currently valued at EUR 1.95 billion." "The purpose of the acquisition of Cymer is to accelerate the development of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) semiconductor lithography technology." (ASML press release, 2012-10-17)
notes: Value is at announcement ('currently valued'); terms US$20.00 cash + 1.1502 ASML shares per Cymer share. Deal closed in 2013 (ASML Cymer page: 'ASML acquired Cymer in 2013').

original_interpretation: At the deal ASML said it would run Cymer as an independent US division, supply sources at arm's length, and keep scanners compatible with all light sources.
evidence_found: "ASML intends to manage Cymer's commercial operations as an independent division based in the United States, and will continue to deliver and service DUV and EUV sources for all customers on an arm's length basis. ASML scanners will continue to interface with light sources from all manufacturers." (2012-10-17)
notes: Stated intention in 2012; whether it held later is not evidenced here.

original_interpretation: Cymer installed base ~3,750 light-source systems at time of deal.
evidence_found: "Cymer's light sources have been widely adopted by the world's top chipmakers and the company's installed base comprises approximately 3,750 systems." (About Cymer, ASML press release 2012-10-17)
notes: Company boilerplate, correctly reported_claim; as of Oct 2012.

original_interpretation: ASML: Cymer is an independently operated business in the ASML group making/servicing DUV (ArF, KrF excimer) light sources, centred in San Diego.
evidence_found: "Cymer is an independently operated business within the ASML group that develops, manufactures and services deep-ultraviolet (DUV) light sources" ... "excimer lasers using argon fluoride (ArF) or krypton fluoride (KrF) gases" ... "Research, development and manufacturing of DUV light sources is centered in San Diego." (asml.com Cymer page)
notes: The lead sentence only appears in the rendered page (read via browser), not in web_extract output.

original_interpretation: Nikon sold 27 semiconductor litho systems (new + refurbished) in FY to Mar-2026: 20 i-line, 4 KrF, 3 ArF dry, 0 ArFi.
evidence_found: Table 6 'Unit Sales of Nikon Semiconductor Lithography Systems by Technology (One Unit)', FY2026/3 1H/total: "i-line, etc. ... 8 20", "KrF ... 0 4", "ArF ... 1 3", "ArF imm. ... 0 0"; table 4 total "9 27"; "Unit sales include refurbished lithography systems." (Nikon data sheet, 2026-05-08)
notes: Sum 20+4+3+0=27. 'i-line, etc.' includes Mini Step & Repeat systems (per Nikon deck note).

original_interpretation: Of Nikon's 27 semiconductor litho units in FY2025/26, 22 new and 5 refurbished.
evidence_found: Table 4 (semiconductor rows): "New Products 4 18 8 22", "Refurbished Products 6 10 1 5", "Total 10 28 9 27" (FY2025/3 1H, total; FY2026/3 1H, total)
notes: Matches Nikon's FY2026/3 results deck note: "The unit sales of new semiconductor lithography systems are ... 22 units in FY2026/3".

original_interpretation: Nikon sold 28 semi litho systems in FY to Mar-2025 (18 i-line, 2 KrF, 5 ArF dry, 3 ArFi), down from 46 in FY2023/24 (11 ArFi).
evidence_found: Table 6: "i-line, etc. 5 23 7 18", "KrF 0 4 0 2", "ArF 3 8 2 5", "ArF imm. 6 11 1 3" (FY2024/3 1H, total; FY2025/3 1H, total); table 4 total "14 46 10 28" (Nikon data sheet, 2025-05-08)
notes: Both totals include refurbished units.

original_interpretation: Inference: Nikon ArFi sales 11 (FY23/24) -> 3 (FY24/25) -> 0 (FY25/26) vs 131 ASML ArFi in CY2025.
notes: Inference follows. Caveats: different fiscal periods; Nikon counts include refurbished; ASML's 131 is net system sales units (new + used).

original_interpretation: Nikon estimated semi litho market ~625 units CY2024 (and ~600 CY2023), forecast ~570 for CY2025.
evidence_found: FY2025/3 deck p. 8: "Semiconductor Lithography Systems (New/Refurbished, units) Market Scale 520 600 625 (CY23/24) Nikon 31/15 18/10 18/10" under columns FY24/3 Actual, FY25/3 Forecast (Feb. 6), FY25/3 Actual; p. 18: "Market Scale 625 570 (CY24/25)".
correction: CY2023 market scale was 520 units, not 600 (600 was the Feb-2025 forecast for CY2024). The CY2025 forecast of 570 has since been reported as the CY2025 figure; Nikon now forecasts 580 for CY2026.
notes: 625 (CY2024) and the 570 forecast are confirmed. The 600 is not CY2023: the Nikon column 31/15 (=46, Nikon's FY2024/3 actual) shows the first column is the CY2023 actual (520) and 600 was Nikon's Feb-2025 forecast for CY2024. Newer data: Nikon's FY2026/3 deck (2026-05-08) reports CY2025 at 570 (actual) and forecasts 580 for CY2026 (new claims in this batch).

original_interpretation: Nikon booked JPY 14.1 bn one-time costs in Precision Equipment FY2024/25 after revising litho plans on major customers' changed investment plans.
evidence_found: "Forward-looking plans for the Semiconductor Lithography Business have been revised given changes to major customers' investment plans and a delayed recovery in the semiconductor market" ... "one-time costs (¥14.1B: fixed-asset impairment losses, inventory write-downs, and restructuring costs related to the optimization of service bases)" (FY2025/3 deck, p. 8)
notes: p. 28 breakdown: impairment -7.8, inventory write-downs -5.0, service-base restructuring -1.2 (JPY bn), all booked in Q4.

original_interpretation: Nikon jointly developing ArFi system with a major chipmaker and a back-end digital litho system, aiming to substantially improve earnings ~2030.
evidence_found: "Meanwhile, forward-looking development (joint development with a major semiconductor maker on ArF immersion lithography system and the development of digital lithography system for back-end processes) will be continued and aim to substantially improve earnings around 2030" (FY2025/3 deck, p. 18)
notes: Plan statement as of May 2025.

original_interpretation: Nikon sells 'EUV related components' in Components; FY2024/25 revenue fell partly on lower sales of these.
evidence_found: "Revenue and profit declined as sales growth in X-ray and CT systems for aerospace applications could not overcome the effects of decreased sales in EUV related components, optical parts and optical components, and encoders" (FY2025/3 deck, p. 10); p. 24 lists "EUV related component" under Components Business.

original_interpretation: Canon aims to sell 71 KrF units in 2026 (+25 vs 2025), citing rising AI-driven orders for memory manufacturing, while i-line for automotive power devices declines with slower EV demand.
evidence_found: "In 2026, we expect the sales of i-line equipment for power semiconductor devices for automotive applications to decline, largely due to the slowdown in EV demand. However, supported by strong AI demand, there has been a significant increase in business negotiations for equipment used in the manufacturing of memory devices. Accordingly, we aim to achieve sales growth by selling 71 KrF units, which is 25 units more than last year." (Canon AR 2025, Industrial Group, p. 21)
correction: Canon cites a 'significant increase in business negotiations' for memory-device equipment, not rising orders.
notes: Units confirmed by the FY2025 results deck slide 20 (KrF 46 in 2025, 71 projected 2026).

original_interpretation: Canon: back-end (packaging) litho sales rose strongly in 2025 on AI demand; claims they set the industry standard for leading-edge packaging.
evidence_found: "As for semiconductor lithography equipment, supported by strong AI-related demand, we posted a large increase in the sales of our equipment used in back-end process applications, which set the industry standard for leading-edge semiconductor packaging." (Canon AR 2025, Industrial Group, p. 21)
notes: 'Industry standard' is Canon's own claim; no unit or value figure is given.

original_interpretation: Canon capex JPY 262.2 bn in 2025, incl. new Utsunomiya semiconductor litho plant.
evidence_found: "We invested 262.2 billion yen in capital expenditure for future growth, including the construction of a new plant at our production site in Utsunomiya for semiconductor lithography equipment, an area where further growth is expected." (Canon AR 2025, To Our Shareholders, p. 3)
notes: The figure is group-wide capex; the plant's share is not stated (the metric population says this correctly).

original_interpretation: Canon AR 2025: specs of NIL equipment shipped to major chipmakers confirmed; mass-production evaluation being accelerated; no mass-production adoption reported.
evidence_found: "As for Nanoimprint, our next-generation semiconductor manufacturing equipment, the specifications of equipment that was shipped to major semiconductor manufacturers were confirmed. We are now working to further accelerate the evaluation and verification of this equipment for use in mass production." (Canon AR 2025, p. 21)
notes: Same page: "we are already shipping systems to customers, and the on-site evaluation of this equipment for use in mass production is progressing smoothly." No mass-production adoption is stated anywhere in the Industrial section.

original_interpretation: Canon sold 234 semi litho units in 2025 (188 i-line, 46 KrF); plans 224 in 2026 (153 i-line, 71 KrF).
evidence_found: Slide 20 'Lithography Equipment (Units)': "Semiconductor KrF 15 46 71", "i-line 58 188 153", "73 234 224", "FPD 8 33 20" (columns 2025 4Q, 2025 FY, 2026 FY Projection; Canon FY2025 results, 2026-01-29)
notes: Read from the PDF text layer (macOS PDFKit), not a chart image. The 2026 figure is a projection.

original_interpretation: Canon released FPA-1200NZ2C NIL in Oct 2023; stamps the pattern rather than projecting; claims 14 nm min linewidth ~5 nm node.
evidence_found: "Canon became the first in the world to commercialize a semiconductor manufacturing system that uses NIL technology ... when it released the FPA-1200NZ2C on October 13, 2023." ... "by pressing a mask imprinted with the circuit pattern into the resist on the wafer like a stamp" ... "enables patterning with a minimum linewidth of 14 nm, equivalent to the 5 nm node" (Canon release, 2024-09-26)

original_interpretation: Canon shipped an FPA-1200NZ2C to the Texas Institute for Electronics on 26 Sep 2024 for R&D and prototypes.
evidence_found: "Canon Inc. announced today that it will ship its most advanced lithography platform, the FPA-1200NZ2C nanoimprint lithography (NIL) system ... to the Texas Institute for Electronics (TIE) ... on September 26, 2024." ... "This FPA-1200NZ2C will be used at TIE for the research and development of advanced semiconductors and production of prototypes."
notes: Shipment announced the same day; delivery itself is not separately confirmed.
